body:
Follow-up to the #473 test findings; part of #454 (Tasks 1b/1c). Two changes, one theme: the first user-visible signal gets faster, and queued runs stop being evictable by noise.

## Fast acknowledgement (inline, no committed JS)

New first step in the router portal — before checkout and runtime setup — posts the 👀 via REST using only `jq` + `gh` on raw payload fields (`github.token` identity). A ~4-line sed/grep pair approximates the boundary-aware live-mention check (fenced code, inline code, quoted lines ignored); `extract-context` remains the authoritative validator, and a `reacted` output suppresses the later resolved-identity reaction so two accounts never both react. Edited events, discussions, and PR review bodies keep the post-setup path (new-mention validation / GraphQL-only surfaces). Expected ack: ~15–20s → **~5–7s** (runner pickup + one API call). Script smoke-tested against synthetic payloads: live mention reacts; fenced/quoted/inline-code mentions, unsupported surfaces, and missing IDs all fall through cleanly.

## Eviction-safe concurrency

Root cause from issue #473: GitHub keeps at most **one pending run per concurrency group** and cancels the previous pending run whenever a newer one queues. Sepo's own progress-comment edits fire `issue_comment edited` webhooks into the same per-issue group as real runs, so during any active run, noise events chain-cancel whatever is pending — including a queued human mention (observed as the chain of cancelled runs 29183691633…29183709008).

- **Entrypoint**: bot-sender events divert to `agent-noise-<run_id>` throwaway groups; human events key on the triggering comment/review ID when present (#454 Task 1c — mentions in different comments now run concurrently), with per-target fallback for comment-less surfaces where newest-edit-wins is the intended dedupe.
- **Label workflow**: bot labelers (Sepo's status label) *and* non-`agent/*` labels divert to throwaway groups — any random label was another eviction vector.
- **Prerequisite lock**: `agent-fix-pr.yml` gains a job-level `agent-fix-pr-job-<pr>` group, because workflow-level concurrency is not applied via `workflow_call` (a distinct name from the workflow-level group, which would self-deadlock standalone dispatches). Known, documented trade: parallel answer runs on one target may race session-bundle registration (resume-best-effort ⇒ reduced continuity, not corruption).

## Validation

Envelope tests pin the new invariants (fast_ack before checkout + suppression wiring, noise-group expressions, distinct fix-pr job lock): workflow lane 90/90, docs 5/5, shell 15/15. CHANGELOG updated under Unreleased.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #474 follows #473 and implements Tasks 1b/1c of #454. It adds a pre-checkout 👀 reaction using raw webhook data, diverts noise events into unique concurrency groups, and keys human comments independently. It also adds a job-level fix-PR lock for reusable-workflow calls. The goal is faster acknowledgement without allowing noise events to evict legitimate queued work.

## Review

The noise diversion and distinct fix-PR lock are directionally correct, but the current head introduces a concrete race for mutating routes. The fast acknowledgement and queue handling also need tightening before merge.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Unlocked mutating routes can race | BLOCKING | [Per-comment grouping](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/90447ca3c49525dfed3910bcdf1566028b376972/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml#L39-L59) releases the previous target lock before routing, while `/install` and mutation-capable `skill` runs have no replacement. Concurrent installs can publish the fixed `agent/install-agent-infra` branch and race or fail non-fast-forward. |
| Fast acknowledgement overmatches invalid handles | WARNING | [`grep -qF`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/90447ca3c49525dfed3910bcdf1566028b376972/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L193-L202) accepts strings such as `@sepo-agentic`, unlike the canonical boundary-aware parser. This posts a misleading 👀 before authoritative validation declines the trigger. |
| Serialized write queues can still drop requests | WARNING | The new fix-PR lock and existing implement lock retain the single-pending default, so a third request replaces the second. GitHub now supports non-lossy `queue: max` groups of up to 100 pending runs. [GitHub concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) |
| Fast API call lacks an explicit duration bound | WARNING | The first [`gh api` call](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/90447ca3c49525dfed3910bcdf1566028b376972/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L198-L204) has no step or subprocess timeout and suppresses diagnostics. `continue-on-error` preserves fallback only after the command terminates. |

## Progress

- Current head `90447ca3c49525dfed3910bcdf1566028b376972` is mergeable, [Test Scripts passes](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/29184101259), and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Documentation, changelog coverage, noise diversion, and distinct fix-PR workflow/job group names are already present.
- The matcher and single-pending queue findings were already covered by the existing rubrics comment, so no duplicate inline feedback was posted.
- Posted one new inline comment for the unlocked install race: [discussion_r3565897639](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/474#discussion_r3565897639). No comments were replied to, minimized, or resolved.
- The proposed association-gating finding was not carried forward: all standard GitHub associations are accepted by context extraction, and the existing late reaction already precedes route-level access-policy resolution.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Unlocked mutating routes can race</summary>

**Cause:** `/install` runs directly inside the router without concurrency protection and publishes through an ordinary push to a fixed branch. Repository skills also run with write-capable credentials and `approve-all`.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a `queue: max` job lock keyed by the source target for `/install`, and either similarly serialize `skill` runs or explicitly constrain them to read-only behavior.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered the concurrency work ship-ready; an independent route audit found this regression, and the current code confirms it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fast acknowledgement overmatches invalid handles</summary>

**Cause:** The fast path uses literal substring matching while `mentions.ts` requires leading and trailing token boundaries. The new tests inspect workflow text but never execute the matcher.

**Candidate solutions:** Implement a literal-safe boundary matcher and add executable fixtures for valid/invalid boundaries, code and quote stripping, supported endpoints, API failure, and fallback.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed on severity. This synthesis uses WARNING because authoritative validation still prevents route execution; the impact is a misleading reaction rather than an unauthorized action.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Serialized write queues can still drop requests</summary>

**Cause:** `cancel-in-progress: false` does not change the default `queue: single`; only one pending request is retained.

**Candidate solutions:** Add `queue: max` to both fix-PR locks, the implement lock, and any new install/skill mutation locks. Extend envelope tests to assert this invariant.

**Comments:** Reviewers rated this between WARNING and BLOCKING. It requires three overlapping requests, but silently losing accepted work warrants correction.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fast API call lacks an explicit duration bound</summary>

**Cause:** The best-effort API request has neither a step timeout nor a bounded subprocess wrapper, and stderr is discarded.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a short explicit timeout, preserve a concise failure diagnostic, and verify that timeout/failure leaves `reacted=false` so the established reaction path remains available.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The blocking route-lock regression and remaining fast-path and queue issues are concrete, localized branch changes suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items

- [ ] Add non-lossy per-target serialization for `/install` and audit/lock mutation-capable `skill` runs.
- [ ] Enforce canonical mention boundaries and add executable fast-ack regression tests.
- [ ] Add `queue: max` to both fix-PR locks, `agent-implement`, and the new mutation locks.
- [ ] Bound the fast acknowledgement API call while preserving fallback behavior and concise diagnostics.

---
`codex` | `gpt-5.6-sol[max]` | `Macmini-runner-2`

All four review action items are addressed in ad3ce02:

- **Mutation-route locks (blocking):** router `install` and `skill` jobs gained per-source-target `queue: max` concurrency groups — serialization chosen over read-only constraint for skills, since repo-defined skills legitimately mutate.
- **Boundary matcher:** the fast ack now enforces `mentions.ts`-style boundaries (leading start/whitespace/`(`, trailing terminator/end), so a handle with a trailing suffix no longer matches. The new `.agent/scripts/test/fast-ack.test.cjs` extracts the step script from the workflow YAML and executes it against fixtures — boundary overmatch, fence/inline/quote stripping, endpoint selection per surface, missing IDs, unsupported surfaces, and API failure → `reacted=false` with a diagnostic.
- **Non-lossy queues:** `queue: max` added to both fix-pr locks, the implement lock, and the new install/skill locks; envelope tests pin the invariant. One caveat: the concurrency docs only show `queue` at workflow level explicitly — it's applied here at job level too (fix-pr job, install, skill), so the first post-merge `/fix-pr` run is worth watching; if GitHub rejects job-level `queue`, the fallback is dropping that one key while keeping the job-level groups.
- **Bounded ack call:** `gh api` replaced with `curl --max-time 10` inside a `timeout-minutes: 1` step, failure diagnostics logged concisely, `reacted=false` preserved on any failure so the post-setup reaction path remains available.

Lanes: workflow 91/91, shell 18/18, runtime 756/756, docs 5/5.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #474 follows the queue-eviction behavior observed in #473 and implements Tasks 1b/1c of #454. It moves the 👀 acknowledgement before checkout, isolates noise events, keys human comments independently, and adds non-lossy locks for mutating routes. At current head `ad3ce02`, the previous handle-boundary, queue-depth, and timeout findings are fixed with executable coverage. Two localized correctness gaps remain in install serialization and Markdown-fence handling.

## Review

The overall design is sound, the required check passes, and the PR is mergeable. The remaining findings are warnings rather than blockers, but both warrant small branch changes.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Install lock keys the source thread, not the external target | WARNING | The [install concurrency group](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ad3ce0206355127394e60a259a73d7928a1bf004/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L882-L888) differs across source issues, even when both runs target and push the same external repository branch. One push can consequently fail non-fast-forward and be misreported as a permission failure. |
| List-nested fences can produce false acknowledgements | WARNING | The [fast matcher](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ad3ce0206355127394e60a259a73d7928a1bf004/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L194-L198) only opens fenced ranges when the delimiter begins the line, unlike the canonical parser. Mentions inside list-nested backtick or tilde fences therefore receive 👀 before authoritative validation rejects them. |

## Progress

- Current head `ad3ce0206355127394e60a259a73d7928a1bf004` is mergeable and the `check` workflow succeeds.
- The prior suffix-boundary, single-pending queue, mutation-lock, and unbounded-request findings are substantially addressed.
- Current [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) explicitly supports `queue: max` for jobs and workflow runs, resolving the reviewer concern about job-level schema support.
- Added a [same-agent reply](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/474#discussion_r3565954435) clarifying the residual install race and opened a [new inline comment](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/474#discussion_r3565954454) for nested fences. No comments were minimized and no threads were resolved.
- The stale “`jq + gh`” source comment and label-workflow wording are optional INFO nits and are intentionally excluded from required action items.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Install lock keys the source thread, not the external target</summary>

**Cause:** The lock uses the source issue/PR kind and number, while `/install` later resolves an external repository and pushes its fixed `agent/install-agent-infra` branch. Different source issues can therefore receive different locks while sharing the protected branch.

**Candidate solutions:** Key concurrency on the normalized external target, or conservatively serialize all install jobs. Add coverage for two source issues requesting the same external repository.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed because the new lock restores the previous same-source serialization. The current helper confirms that cross-source requests can still converge on the same branch, so this remains a narrower WARNING.

</details>

<details>
<summary>List-nested fences can produce false acknowledgements</summary>

**Cause:** Fence deletion requires leading whitespace before the delimiter, while `stripNonLiveMentions()` removes paired triple-backtick and tilde fences wherever they occur. Executing the current matcher against list-nested fixtures produced `fast=true` and `canonical=false`.

**Candidate solutions:** Make the fast fence filter conservative for delimiters anywhere on a line and add list-nested backtick and tilde fixtures to `fast-ack.test.cjs`.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered this cosmetic and rare; another demonstrated the parity failure. Authoritative extraction prevents route execution, limiting the impact to misleading acknowledgement.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: Both warnings are concrete, localized workflow-and-test changes suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict

MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items

- [ ] Key `/install` serialization to the external target resource, or serialize all install jobs, with a cross-source regression invariant.
- [ ] Align fast fence stripping conservatively with the canonical parser and add list-nested backtick and tilde fixtures.

---
